text:
Alex: FYI onboarding sampleapp02 hit a weird hang on the generation step. UI progress bar never updates, it just jumps at the end. curl streaming works fine. Anyone seen streaming differences between REST and the Node SDK?
Hanna: paste the curl + sdk snippet?
Alex: curl that streams fine:
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","prompt":"stream test","stream":true}'
```
Alex: Node SDK (observed behavior):
```js
const s = client.generate.stream({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', prompt: 'stream test', stream: true })
for await (const ev of s) {
  // only one event emitted at the end, not incremental tokens
  ui.append(ev.text)
}
```
Omar: Did you capture the raw HTTP responses from both?
Hanna: Yes 10 I grabbed tcpdump + node fetch logs. Server sends multiple SSE events (lines starting `data:`) about every 40-80ms. curl prints them live. The Node SDK's http client appears to buffer and emit only on end.
Leah: That sounds like the Node wrapper is using a non-streaming path for some Node versions (internal fetch fallback that calls response.text()) and so we lose incremental chunks. Which SDK version?
Alex: We're on node-sdk 3.2.1 using the default runtime fetch polyfill. On Node 18 in the onboarding container.
Omar: We changed the fetch-wrapper in 3.2.0 to unify browser/server behavior. It falls back to response.text() when the stream reader isn't detected in the env. Looks like the CI container doesn't expose the streaming reader shape we expect and the wrapper picks the buffered path.
Hanna: Workaround for ops: use raw fetch in the container or the low-level `client.requestStream(...)` experimental binding that exposes the underlying response body reader. Using raw `fetch` with `response.body.getReader()` shows the tokens live and the progress bar works.
Alex: Confirmed workaround: `await client.raw.fetch('/v1/generate', { headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream' }, body: JSON.stringify({...}) })` then read body via reader. UI updates normally.
Leah: Longer-term fix: detect streaming-capable runtime shapes more robustly, and prefer ReadableStream/streaming reader APIs instead of buffered fallback. Also add an integration e2e that runs a tiny streaming generation and verifies incremental events in CI.
Omar: I'll open a hotfix to prefer streaming on Node >= 16 and add an env-smoke to onboarding CI to catch regressions. We should also document the `client.raw.fetch` workaround in devex onboarding guide until patch lands.
Alex: sdk-bot create issue please and tag onboarding ops.
sdk-bot: Created issue #4005 - \"node-sdk: streaming client buffers SSE and emits only on end in some Node environments\" and attached tcpdump + HAR.
Omar: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/854 - prefer streaming reader when available + add e2e streaming smoke.
Leah: Nice. Please also add test permutations for Node 18/20 and our container base image so we don't regress.
Hanna: Workaround + notes added to the onboarding runbook. New onboard proceeded after using raw fetch. :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks all 10 leaving this thread so new onboarding runs are aware.
